title: Priority queue & slab mapper — Dedicated contract allocations (Nov 2028 snapshot)
summary: Working workbook to map per-contract slabs into a multi-tier priority queue for Dedicated customers. Purpose: produce a deterministic allocator that honors committed GPUs, supports short-term bursts, and provides a transparent fallback order when capacity is constrained.
assumptions: Committed GPUs are nightly-averaged and billed pro-rata (unless explicitly waived in contract).
Burst pools are finite per-region and must be carved from unused committed capacity first.
Priority tiers: platinum (0), gold (1), silver (2), bronze (3). Lower numeric = higher priority.
We reserve 8% of regional capacity for platform overhead and emergency reroutes.
Utilization targets are conservative — aim to keep 72% steady-state utilization across active slabs to allow buffer for canary/fallbacks.

Effective burst budget after reserve: 436 GPUs

calculation_notes: Burst_budget_gpus initially set to 25% of committed_gpus for platinum/gold, 16% for silver, 0% for bronze — adjusted manually where contract states otherwise.
Current_util_pct pulled from last 14-day rolling average (internal metric INF-GPU-UTIL-14D).
If region free capacity < required burst, use cross-region soft-fallback by priority tier; record expected added latency in notes.
playbook_steps: 1) Lock top-priority slabs for the next 90 days (no downsize without account exec approval).
2) Recompute burst budgets weekly based on 7-day empty-slots delta and open commitments.
3) Run dry-run allocator simulation for each production deploy (Jenkins job: allocator/dryrun).
4) For contracts nearing end date, tag slab as 'transition' and plan capacity release 30 days prior.
open_questions: Should we convert fixed burst budgets to elastic credits that roll over monthly? Pros/cons listed in linked Confluence page.
What is acceptable latency delta for cross-region fallback for platinum customers? (proposal: <= 120ms median additional RTT).
Confirm legal on billing for emergency platform reserve usage (when we dip into reserve for failover).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: sustained oversubscription in us-west1 during new model launches. Mitigation: prebook temporary cloud partner capacity and throttle low-priority slabs.
Risk: contract mis-sync (sales vs ledger). Mitigation: weekly reconciliation spreadsheet (Finance-owned).
Risk: sudden regional outage reduces effective capacity by >30%. Mitigation: automated reroute to secondary region for platinum/gold with consumer notice cadence.
